chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Lucky Roberts calls him to New York
summary: Broke in Boston, he is called by Lucky Roberts around 1925 to play a society gig on Fifth Avenue, and Hinton notes Roberts held the society gigs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I was paying the lady about $10 a week, I think and didn't have no job, the musicians in New York would say, go on back to Boston, so around '25, the -- Lucky Roberts called me.
He was the great piano player we're talking about. He wrote that song.
He had a club up there, a liquor joint.

Up there at 149th Street and St. Nicholas Avenue and he used to have entertainers and everybody, the waiters were all singers, see, up there and so this night he called me and he asked me was I busy and I said no man, so I got together with him and his singer, see, Charlie Purcell and we went down to 666 Fifth Avenue and there was about six people, three couples and we entertained, played soft music and singing and I got $75 for that gig and that's when I started romping.
They tell me this Lucky Roberts was the society band man of New York in those days.
He had all of the gigs, all of the good gigs, is that so.
